title: Approximate tangent spaces are local: sets that agree near x have the same approximate tangent spaces at x (parent step 4)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let S, S' ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets (no measurability is assumed), x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and δ > 0 with S ∩ B_δ(x) = S' ∩ B_δ(x), where B_δ(x) is the open ball. If Q is the approximate tangent space of S' at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q: dim Q = n, and ∫_{η_{x,r}(S')} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^n = μHE[n]), then Q is also the approximate tangent space of S at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q).
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S S' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → S ∩ ball x δ = S' ∩ ball x δ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S' x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q
